title: Multi-region KEK Orchestrator and Automated Residency Evidence Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating across multiple cloud regions and on-prem sites need auditable proof that their tenant keys (KEKs) are rotated according to policy and that data residency constraints are respected. Current rotation is manual or semi-automated, and evidence generation for compliance audits is ad-hoc and brittle.

Goal: Build a centralized KEK Orchestrator service that coordinates scheduled rotations across cloud KMS providers and HSM gateways, enforces per-tenant residency policies, and emits signed, queryable evidence artifacts suitable for SOC/ISO/PCI reviews. The pipeline should integrate with existing telemetry and the Console reporting UI so security teams can retrieve rotation timelines, residency attestations, and cryptographic proof bundles programmatically.
acceptance_criteria:
- KEK Orchestrator can schedule and trigger rotations in at least two cloud KMS vendors (AWS KMS and GCP KMS) and our on-prem HSM gateway.
- Every successful rotation emits a signed evidence bundle with: rotation timestamp, KEK identifier, nonce, operator ID, resulting key fingerprints, region tag, and proof-of-execution signature.
- Evidence bundles stored in S3-compatible object store with retention metadata and tamper-detection hash; Console exposes search by tenant + time range.
- Automated alerts for failed or partial rotations with retry/backoff and escalation policy.
- End-to-end test harness that simulates multi-region rotation and validates evidence format.
- Security review completed and threat model signed off.
- Documentation: runbook for on-call, PRD section for billing impact, and README for onboarding new KMS/HSM adapters.
implementation_plan:
1) Adapter layer: implement KMS adapters for AWS KMS and GCP KMS (rotateKey API wrappers), plus an HSM gateway client for our on-prem HSM protocol.
2) Coordinator: durable workflow (Temporal) to orchestrate rotations per-tenant with policy evaluation (residency + exclusion windows).
3) Evidence generator: canonical JSON schema for rotation evidence, include SHA-256 of old/new KEK fingerprints, signed by service HSM key (or tenant-held attest key).
4) Storage & indexing: write bundles to encrypted object store with index entries in the ComplianceDB (time, tenant, region, fingerprint).
5) Console/UI: basic search + download artifact endpoint and retention policy controls.
6) Alerting & retries: integrate with PagerDuty and Slack for escalation.
7) Tests: unit tests for adapters, integration tests against test KMS, e2e harness that validates signed evidence.
8) Rollout: dark-launch for a small set of internal tenants, then staged ramp.

Notes on infra: use existing dedicated vault for service signing key with HSM backing; Temporal task queues should be per-region to keep latency predictable.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Chosen Temporal over cron-based scheduling to enable durable workflows and built-in retries; tradeoff is operational complexity and a dependency on Temporal availability.
- Evidence signing will use a service signing key in HSM for non-repudiation rather than trying to collect tenant keys (simpler UX, but we must document threat model and allow tenant-provided attest keys as an opt-in).
- Implement eventual consistency on index entries to avoid blocking KMS backends; evidence is immutable, so index repair jobs will run asynchronously.
- Supporting additional KMS vendors will use a plugin adapter interface to minimize change to core coordinator logic.
